clue.text: Main supporters of retired Naval types?

definitions.text: Main supporters of retired Naval types?

parts.words: Main supporters of retired Naval types
parts.note: the main is the sea; those who serve on it are held up in hanging canvas beds when they retire for the night

explanation.surface: A question about who backs up ex-Navy men in their retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioned off, but it means gone to bed, and 'Main' is the sea, not 'chief'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors traditionally slept slung in canvas beds below deck, so these beds literally supported seafarers at rest.

clue.text: D for Deposit. Greek D for this sort

definitions.text: D for Deposit. Greek D for this sort

parts.words: D for Deposit. Greek D for this sort
parts.note: the Greek letter D is delta, and a river delta is a deposit of the silty kind left by flowing water

explanation.surface: A spelling-alphabet game: D stands for Deposit, and the Greek D for a type.
explanation.walkthrough: Delta, the Greek D, is the triangular silt deposit at a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt laid down by rivers forms deposits such as a delta, described by this adjective.

clue.text: Powerful cocktails they're serving at Wimbledon

definitions.meaning: double measures of spirits mixed into drinks
the tennis event where a man and woman partner each other

explanation.surface: Strong drinks are being handed out at the Wimbledon tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis tournament; 'serving' suggests waiters but means tennis serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is two measures of spirits; in tennis the pairs event with one man and one woman per team.

clue.text: Retain £100 for repair of musical instrument

indicators.note: the letters are mended, that is put back together in a new order

parts.note: £ is L for pound and 100 is the Roman numeral C

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a hundred pounds to fix an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-reed woodwind is a classic musical instrument.

clue.text: One dreaming perhaps about John Hunter's return

indicators.note: the whole run of letters comes back to front

parts.note: re means about or concerning
John Peel was the famous Cumbrian huntsman of the song, so his is Peel's

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of the huntsman John Peel's homecoming.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel is the huntsman of the folk song 'D'ye ken John Peel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep may well be dreaming, so a dreamer is perhaps this.

clue.text: A less than lavish arrangement answers the purpose

indicators.note: the remaining letters are arranged into a new order
the word lavish falls short, its final letter cut

explanation.surface: A modest arrangement still does the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' trims the last letter of the clue's lavish word, and 'arrangement' shuffles what is left, placed after the plain A.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of use or serve a purpose is the verb sense of 'avail'.

clue.text: Currency discount one obtained in past

indicators.note: the one is got into the middle of the past word

parts.note: ago means in the past
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone once got a discount on foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is used for the percentage charged on exchanging currency, a premium or discount.

clue.text: Despairing advice, from pessimist?

definitions.meaning: a gloomy adviser might tell you to ...

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy gives advice in a despairing tone.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as 'hope less' for the pessimist's advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in despair means having lost all expectation of improvement.

clue.text: Borrow book shown as £5—on gear-changing

indicators.note: the letters of the gear are being changed about, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: £ is L (libra, pound) and 5 is the Roman numeral V
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book is priced at five pounds, apparently connected with changing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' is George Borrow, the Victorian author; the anagram indicator 'changing' rearranges LV, ON and GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow wrote the semi-autobiographical novel about a Romany-loving scholar, published 1851.

clue.text: Careless, following start of fire in the plant

indicators.note: the slack piece comes after the opening letter, as the clue orders it
the beginning of the word fire supplies only its initial letter

parts.note: lax means careless or slack

explanation.surface: Someone careless in the factory caused a fire to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the plant' reads as a factory; the plant is the definition, the fibre crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is a blue-flowered crop grown for linen fibre and linseed.

clue.text: Notes made at work

parts.note: notes here are banknotes, the money you get paid for a job rather than jottings in a meeting

explanation.surface: Someone jots down memos during the working day.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages and salaries are income gained through employment, as opposed to investment returns.

clue.text: Study card groups in game

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
sequences are runs of consecutive cards

explanation.surface: Players examine sets of cards during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Con, meaning study, is an old word; the game is the parlour game of folded-paper stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper-folding parlour game where players add story lines unseen is a well-known party game.

clue.text: Barnes's ale mixed with this lime

definitions.meaning: William Barnes, the Dorset poet, wrote the song whose title is this tree name followed by ALE rearranged, LEA
the lime tree, also called by its German-derived name

explanation.surface: A poet's beer is blended with a squeeze of lime.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: rearrange ALE to LEA, and put this word before it to get Barnes's poem 'Linden Lea', a famous English song.
explanation.definitionFit: The lime tree of Europe, genus Tilia, has a second name taken from German, the one in the Unter den tree avenue.

clue.text: Is on reel made from scene of Hamlet

indicators.note: something new is built out of these letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film of Hamlet is on the reel, made from the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare sets the Danish play at the royal castle at Helsingør, Denmark.

clue.text: Shows off homes, including one abroad

indicators.note: the homes take the foreign one into their middle

parts.note: flats are homes
un is French for one

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about owning houses, one of them overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something ostentatiously is to show it off.

clue.text: Pools investment for oriental actors

parts.note: E stands for east, the oriental direction
a cast is a body of actors

explanation.surface: Football pools money is put up for Asian performers.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game on match results; your entry is a predicted set of results.
explanation.definitionFit: A pools coupon is filled with predictions of match results, the entry staked.

clue.text: Seems to yield fruit in spring, though backward

indicators.note: the fruit sits inside the turned spring
the spring word runs from right to left

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Something appears to bear fruit in springtime, if late in the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season but is a mineral water resort; 'though backward' turns it, and the fruit goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give the appearance of something, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Quietly wander about in many a region

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: the wander word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: rove means wander
C is a hundred in Roman numerals, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Someone strolls softly around a great many places in a region.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or territorial division of a country is a region.

clue.text: He argues one's damaged in back

indicators.note: the damaged letters sit inside the back

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: the letters of the word are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man claims he was injured in the back.
explanation.definitionFit: One who argues logically from premises, the person who reasons.

clue.text: Fall is modest-about a point

indicators.note: the modest word goes round the point

parts.note: decent means modest or proper
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: The fall is restrained, around a point in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop or downward movement from higher to lower is a synonym noun.

clue.text: Wheel on the road to fortune ?

definitions.text: Wheel on the road to fortune ?

parts.words: Wheel on the road to fortune
parts.note: not a vehicle's wheel but the spinning casino wheel gamblers hope will make them rich

explanation.surface: A car wheel rolls along the highway towards riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino game is played on a numbered spinning wheel on which gamblers stake their money.

clue.text: Arrangement of slates that could be ornamental

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for the noun: a thing that may serve as an ornament

indicators.note: the letters of the roof material are set out anew

explanation.surface: Roof slates laid in a pattern can look decorative.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging bunch of threads knotted at one end is a decorative trimming.

clue.text: It's a sort of demonstration you see

definitions.text: It's a sort of demonstration you see

parts.words: It's a sort of demonstration you see
parts.note: a demonstration you see with your eyes, the kind Othello demanded as proof

explanation.surface: A protest is explained to a listener, 'you see' being a mere aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you see' sounds conversational but is literal: the demonstration is by sight, as in Othello's 'ocular proof'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the eyes or sight, as in a visible demonstration.

clue.text: Peevish lot of Gallup's victims ?

parts.note: cross means peevish or irritable
a lot or portion is a section

explanation.surface: Grumpy are the folk polled by the Gallup organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Gallup is the polling firm; its 'victims' are the representative sample it questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollster surveys a representative sample of the population, chosen to reflect every group.

clue.text: Said to be virtuous, but no leader

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word, is taken away

parts.note: moral means virtuous

explanation.surface: Someone is reputed to be good, but lacks a figurehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, the sense of an exam described as by mouth.

clue.text: Inclination to unctuous hypocrisy

explanation.surface: A tendency towards oily two-faced talk.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a slant or bevel; the other is insincere moralising language.

clue.text: Has ordered fresh supply of leather

indicators.note: the three letters are put in a new order

parts.note: green means fresh or new

explanation.surface: Someone has ordered a new stock of leather goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagreen is a granular untanned leather, often of shark or horse skin, dyed green.

clue.text: What could be, say, truer as a description of Palgrave's work ?

indicators.note: these letters could become another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a review of a Palgrave book could be more accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Palgrave edited 'The Golden Treasury', the famous Victorian anthology of English verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The anthology's title names a store of riches, part of the name of his collection.
